mutations.because: The defect this lane fixes, restored: every write succeeds whatever revision the caller read, so the second of two overlapping read-modify-write sequences overwrites the first and its edit is gone with no error. The unconditional write is exactly what the ECONFLICT guard replaces.

Every write failure becomes a 409 with the pool's current revision, so a disk error is reported to HITL as 'someone else edited this' — the route would claim a conflict it never detected. The 500-vs-409 split is what the read-only-directory test pins.
GET stops handing out the revision, so no caller can ever send one and the conditional write on the port is unreachable from the web client — the revision would exist on the port and nowhere else.
The client reads the revision and then never sends it back, so the server's guard never sees one: the conditional write is decorative and the lost update this lane removes survives the whole feature.
